newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ manufacturers urge Peters not to overspend.
newsitem.headline: NZ manufacturers urge Peters not to overspend.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer Winston Peters is now in a position to bring down the value of the dollar as he pledged during last year's election campaign, the New Zealand Manufacturers' Federation said on Monday.
ManFed said the value of the dollar was now in the hands of Peters, who holds the positions of Treasurer and deputy prime minister in the centre-right coalition government.

"He has the choice of using any savings his razor gang might find in the current 1997/98 budget to increase expenditure on coalition policies beyond the NZ$1.2 billion already earmarked, or he could stick the money in the bank," ManFed said in a
"If he spends it he will further put upward pressure on the dollar. He will be selling exporters down the river. But if he saves it he will help bring the dollar down."
ManFed said not all of the coalition spending policies had been well thought through and many could do with "more measured consideration".
"It would be a bad mistake to throw hard earned savings at these lower priority policies, when banking the savings will definitely help build a stronger economy."
